title: Equivalent Fractions and Ordering Fractions
seo_title: Equivalent and Ordering Fractions – Primary 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify equivalent fractions using diagrams; compare and order fractions using > and <. (summary of the NERDC Primary 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 maths worksheets on equivalent fractions with pictures and comparing and ordering fractions with > and <. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Same top number: fewer parts is bigger.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Equivalent fractions show the same amount: 1/2 of a bar is the same as 2/4 of the same bar.
  • When the bottom numbers are the same, the bigger top number is the bigger fraction: 3/5 > 2/5.
  • When the top numbers are the same, the smaller bottom number is the bigger fraction: 1/3 > 1/6.

Examples

Example

Compare 1/4 and 1/6

Fourths are bigger than sixths

Answer: 1/4 > 1/6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking 1/8 > 1/4 because 8 > 4More pieces means each piece is smaller.
Using different-sized wholesCompare fractions of the same whole.
Thinking 2/4 is more than 1/2They are equal.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Samuel eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza does he eat?
items.e: The pizza has 8 equal slices, so the denominator is 8. Samuel eats 3, so the answer is 38.

items.q: A bar of chocolate has 5 equal pieces. Yetunde eats 2 pieces. What fraction of the bar is left?
items.e: 5 − 2 = 3 pieces are left out of 5 equal pieces. The answer is 35.

items.q: There are 30 children in a Primary 3 class. 13 of them have school lunch. How many children have school lunch?
items.e: Share 30 into 3 equal groups: 30 ÷ 3 = 10 children. One group is 13.

items.q: Zainab has 20 sweets. 34 of them are red. How many red sweets are there?
items.e: First find 14: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. You need 3 groups, not 1: 5 × 3 = 15 sweets.

items.q: There are 24 pupils in a class. 38 of them go to football club. How many pupils go to football club?
items.e: First find 18: 24 ÷ 8 = 3. You need 3 groups, not 1: 3 × 3 = 9 pupils.

items.q: Tobi eats 14 of a pizza. Kunle eats 16 of a pizza of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: A pizza cut into 4 has bigger slices than a pizza cut into 6. 14 > 16, so Tobi eats more.

items.q: Blessing eats 12 of a sandwich. Ikenna eats 24 of a sandwich of the same size. Who eats more?
